title: Exact spectral integrability of a finite-channel random Schrödinger operator: from fermionization of the Dyson--Riccati gas to Kontsevich integral
authors: Yan V. Fyodorov, Pierre Le Doussal
abstract: We solve exactly, for arbitrary finite channel number $N$, the Riccati dynamics of a quasi-one-dimensional random matrix Schrödinger operator with Hermitian white-noise potential in the $β=2$ unitary symmetry class. The associated Dyson--Riccati eigenvalue gas admits an exact free-fermion representation at any sample length $L$, which in the limit $L\to \infty$ expresses the density of states and the total Lyapunov growth rate exactly through a single Airy Hankel $τ$-function providing multichannel generalization of $N=1$ Halperin--Thouless formulas. The $τ-$function further admits an outgoing-contour Kontsevich matrix Airy integral representation. Its saddle-point and double-scaling analyses give, in a unified way, the finite-channel density Lifshitz tail, and the large-$N$ spectral edge. In particular, for $N\gg 1$ the sharp $N=\infty$ edge is softened within an $N^{-4/5}$ spectral window, with its profile governed by the tritronquée solution of Painlevé I. We conjecture universality of this quasi-one-dimensional scaling edge profile for a broad class of $β=2$ random band matrices.
summary: This work provides an exact solution for the spectral properties of a finite-channel random Schrödinger operator by mapping its dynamics to a free-fermion system. Key results include expressing the density of states via an Airy Hankel determinant and determining the universal scaling profile of the spectral edge using Painlevé I solutions. This offers deep theoretical insight into spectral statistics in disordered quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper solves exactly the Riccati dynamics associated with a quasi-one-dimensional random Schrödinger operator for arbitrary finite channel number N.
main_result: The system's spectral properties, including the density of states and Lyapunov growth rate, are determined by an Airy Hankel $\tau$-function, which exhibits universal scaling near the spectral edge governed by Painlevé I.
method: The analysis maps the problem to free fermions, utilizing determinantal formulas (Hankel determinants) and employing saddle-point approximations and large-N limits.
model_or_system: The model is an N-channel random Schrödinger operator with a white-noise potential, whose dynamics are governed by the Riccati equation. The system is analyzed in the $\beta=2$ unitary symmetry class.
key_observables: Inverse Density of States (IDOS), total Lyapunov growth rate, one-point density $n(\lambda)$, and the spectral edge profile.
important_parameters: Finite channel number $N$, sample length $L$, and the symmetry parameter $\beta=2$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of a global projective boundary condition and the validity of the free-fermion representation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the finite-N Lifshitz tail below the spectral edge and compare the finite-N density to the $N=\infty$ mean-field density.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from solving the Riccati dynamics to finding the free-fermion representation, deriving the spectral density via Hankel determinants, and finally analyzing the critical behavior near the spectral edge using Painlevé equations.
why_interesting: The connection between random matrix theory, integrable systems (Painlevé equations), and spectral statistics provides powerful, exact tools for understanding localization and spectral rigidity in disordered quantum systems, which is highly relevant to AMO physics.
